e: A $1.9 billion IMF loan is approved by the Plurinational Legislative Assembly.
Nine people are killed in a fireworks explosion at a military base in Viacha.
A light aircraft of the Bolivian Air Force crashes during aerial patrols over a blockaded highway between La Paz and Cochabamba, killing six officers.
President Paz declares a state of emergency in response to nationwide antigovermnent protests and road blockades.
President Paz signs a law easing the government's ability to declare a state of emergency.
Public works minister Mauricio Zamora survives two separate ambushes on his vehicle by protesters in Copata.
President Paz repeals a law allowing for the mortgaging of land amid widespread protests.
A bus overturns near Oruro, killing nine people and injuring 22 others.
A bus plunges into a ravine in Apolo, La Paz, killing six people and injuring 14 others.

Authorities arrest suspected Uruguayan drug cartel leader Sebastián Marset during a police operation in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Marset, who is wanted by several countries and has a US$2 million reward linked to money laundering allegations, is detained along with four other individuals.

A C-130 Hercules aircraft of the Bolivian Air Force overshoots the runway while landing at El Alto International Airport near La Paz and collides with several vehicles, killing at least 22 people and injuring 29 others.
A nationwide ban on the usage of cellphones in classrooms comes into effect.
A bus crashes in Santa Cruz Department, killing 11 people and injuring three others.
Mauricio Aramayo, an aide to president Paz, is shot dead in Tarija.
